In contrast, MP Materials is already operational with increasing revenue and adjusted positive earnings, providing a more tangible and less risky option for investors seeking exposure to the rare-earth market.

item.title: [AAPL Bearish (-0.29)] Using This Apple Privacy Feature? Researchers Warn It Has a Flaw
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bearish (-0.29)
Researchers have identified a flaw in Apple's Private Relay feature that may inadvertently expose users' IP addresses, even when the feature is enabled. The vulnerability stems from WebKit, Apple's browser engine, and particularly affects users who utilize passkeys, which bypass Private Relay. This issue allows for DNS leaks and the exposure of real IP addresses, contradicting the privacy assurances of Private Relay.

item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.29)
Apple's App Store saw a 0.6% year-over-year revenue increase in the first 35 days of its fiscal fourth quarter, reaching $3.4 billion, despite a 4% decline in total downloads. This growth was driven by a 4.7% increase in dollars per download. Bank of America reiterated a Buy rating on Apple, highlighting strong capital returns, potential AI leadership, and new product optionality, with a price objective of $380.

item.title: [AMZN Bullish (+0.24)] O’Reilly Automotive, suppliers sharing tariff refund benefits
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Bullish (+0.24)
O’Reilly Automotive is sharing the benefits of refunds from now-invalidated tariffs with its suppliers, as its sourcing model primarily relies on suppliers as the importer of record. The auto parts retailer stated that direct tariff rebates are handled through cost of goods negotiations and aims to ensure both O'Reilly and its supplier partners benefit. This approach differs from other retailers like Amazon and Walmart, which plan to return funds to customers or cut prices, and Ford, which will use refunds for business divisions.

item.title: [MSFT Bearish (-0.20)] New York Times Fails to Add Microsoft Claim in OpenAI IP Suit
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bearish (-0.20)
A federal judge denied The New York Times' request to amend its lawsuit against OpenAI to include claims against Microsoft for allegedly encouraging copyright infringement. The judge ruled that the newspaper's attempt to add these theories of contributory infringement was too late, despite a recent US Supreme Court ruling on platform liability. The court noted that The Times could have asserted these claims earlier but chose not to.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.45), AMZN Neutral (-0.11)] Microsoft is starting to show its payoff on major AI plays
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.45), AMZN Neutral (-0.11)
Microsoft is demonstrating a payoff on its AI investments, with growth in its Azure Cloud and Copilot businesses leading to a positive shift in its stock price year-to-date. The company has secured 30 million paid Copilot seats, and Azure growth is accelerating, though a significant portion of its AI revenue is currently attributed to OpenAI. Future growth hinges on sustained Copilot adoption and Azure expansion, as well as Microsoft's ability to diversify its AI revenue streams.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (-0.12)] AquaBounty Eyes Data Center Future for Ohio Site
item.description:

AquaBounty Technologies (NASDAQ: AQB) is exploring strategic alternatives for its dormant Pioneer, Ohio property, including potential data center and power infrastructure development. The site's 50 MW substation connection and 5.25 million-gallon-per-day groundwater permit make it an attractive location for data centers, especially given the current demand for power-rich sites due to AI infrastructure buildout. This move comes as the company continues to divest its salmon farming operations.

item.title: [AMZN Bearish (-0.27)] Amazon sued by Universal Electronics for infringing smart-device patents
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Bearish (-0.27)
Universal Electronics Inc. (UEI) has sued Amazon in California federal court, alleging that Amazon's Echo smart speakers, Fire TV streaming devices, and other products infringe on five of its patents related to remote-control technology. UEI is seeking unspecified monetary damages and an injunction to prevent Amazon from further patent infringement. This lawsuit adds to a history of patent challenges Amazon has faced regarding its Alexa technology, including a $46.7 million judgment in 2023 for infringing speech recognition and natural language processing patents.

item.source: THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

item.title: [TSM Neutral (-0.15)] The Case Against the Proposed Chip Security Act in Taiwan
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Neutral (-0.15)
Taiwan's main opposition party, the Kuomintang (KMT), is proposing legislation that would require legislative approval for certain outbound investments by Taiwanese semiconductor companies. This article argues against this proposal, citing concerns about the constitutional allocation of powers, administrative due process, and the blurring of the relationship between the government and the governed. It suggests that while the legislature has a role in shaping economic security policy, direct involvement in individual investment decisions is institutionally ill-suited for a legislative body.
